citation: This work, KEGG genomic-neighborhood analysis of 60 Bacillota genomes (67 K00096 loci), within-genome random-locus null, 1e5 simulations
claim: The ara-operon placement of the G1P dehydrogenase is conserved beyond B. subtilis
finding: araA/araB/araD within 5 CDS at 20/67 loci vs 0.23 expected (85-fold, p<5e-5); arabinan/arabinofuranosidase genes 31/67 vs 0.55 (56-fold); combined arabinose context at 28/67 loci, 28/60 genomes, 19/38 genera across Bacillus, Shouchella, Niallia, Paenibacillus, Exiguobacterium, Virgibacillus and others
limits: KEGG annotation quality; genus-balanced sampling is not a phylogenetically corrected test, so genera are treated as the independent unit

citation: This work, Needleman-Wunsch global alignment of all 67 K00096 products to AraM (BSU28760, 394 aa)
claim: The arabinose context tracks close orthology, not the whole protein family
finding: Median identity 44.0 % in arabinose context vs 29.8 % elsewhere (Mann-Whitney U=949, p=1.5e-7, CLES 0.87); at a 35 % cut, 28/46 close orthologs are in arabinose context and 0/21 divergent members are (Fisher p=5.2e-7)
limits: Global identity is a coarse orthology proxy; no tree-based reconciliation was run

citation: This work, same neighborhood analysis, pcrB (K07094) channel
claim: The dehydrogenase is adjacent to or co-transcribed with pcrB
finding: 0/67 loci have pcrB within 5 CDS (null expectation 0.14); minimum gene-rank separation 15 overall and 81 among close orthologs, median 1,276; in B. subtilis pcrB (BSU06600, 0.72 Mb) and araM (BSU28760, 2.94 Mb) are 2,258 genes apart
limits: Gene-rank distance ignores operon-independent regulatory coupling

citation: This work, KEGG KO census of 1,717 Bacillota genomes
claim: PcrB requires an AraM-family G1P dehydrogenase
finding: 302 genomes carry K00096, 779 carry K07094, 195 carry both; about 62 % of pcrB-carrying Bacillota have no G1P dehydrogenase of this family
limits: K00096 may miss divergent or non-orthologous G1P dehydrogenases; absence in KEGG is not proof of absence

citation: This work, AraR 16 bp palindrome scan over NC_000964.3:2,937,500-2,950,600 (NCBI efetch)
claim: An AraR operator is present upstream of araM itself, distinct from the operon promoter
finding: Positive controls recovered: 14/16 at 2,948,961 (86 bp upstream of araA, inside the 177 bp abnA/araA intergenic region) and 13/16 upstream of abnA. Zero matches at or above 12/16 anywhere in or around araL, araM or araN
limits: A consensus scan detects canonical operators only; a degenerate or non-AraR site would be missed

citation: This work, intergenic distance calculation across the ara locus
claim: The operon is tightly coupled with no room for an internal promoter upstream of araM
finding: araD/araL overlap by 23 bp, araL/araM overlap by 4 bp, araM/araN gap 30 bp, araN/araP 35 bp, araP/araQ 0 bp, araQ/abfA 18 bp; the largest internal gap in the whole operon is 35 bp, against 177 bp at the promoter-bearing abnA/araA junction
limits: Short intergenic regions do not formally exclude a weak internal promoter; no 5' end mapping or dRNA-seq was retrievable programmatically

citation: This work, intrinsic-terminator scan of the transcribed strand, NC_000964.3:2,937,800-2,949,200 reverse complement, 11,401 nt
claim: An internal terminator uncouples araM from the arabinose-induced transcript
finding: Both positive controls recovered: operon 3' terminator 9 nt after the abfA stop codon, 10 bp GC-rich stem AAGCCGGAGA/TCTCTCCGGCTT, score 27.8 (z=5.14); terminator of the upstream unit, 11 bp stem plus TTTTTTT, score 27.4 (z=5.03). araL/araM scores 14.6 (z=1.54) and araM/araN 16.1 (z=1.95), both at background. Seven of eight internal junctions fall below the mean+4SD cut; the exception, the araD/araL overlap at z=4.27, lies inside araD coding sequence with only 3 U in the following 8 nt and precedes araL, so it cannot uncouple araM specifically
limits: Heuristic inverted-repeat scoring, not an RNA folding calculation, since no folding package was available; cannot detect Rho-dependent termination or RNase processing sites

citation: This work, locus-tag to gene-name verification across the ara locus
claim: The coordinate frame used throughout this report is correct
finding: All nine cistrons are on the minus strand, so locus tags descend along the direction of transcription: araA=BSU28800, araB=BSU28790, araD=BSU28780, araL=BSU28770, araM=BSU28760 (fifth cistron), araN=BSU28750, araP=BSU28740, araQ=BSU28730, abfA=BSU28720. Observed protein lengths match published subunit sizes to within 33 aa (max deviation at araP), all nine intergenic distances reproduce the iteration-1 values exactly, and araA, araM and abfA each begin with ATG on the fetched strand
limits: Expected subunit sizes are taken from the literature record, not re-measured

claim: The operon has a single promoter upstream of araA
finding: One sigma-A dependent promoter maps upstream of araA; transcription of the downstream cistrons depends on it
context: B. subtilis 168, primer extension and transcriptional fusions
limits: Pre-dates genome-wide 5' end mapping; weak internal promoters would not have been detected

claim: AraM is a G1P dehydrogenase with the stated kinetics
finding: Purified AraM reversibly interconverts DHAP and sn-glycerol 1-phosphate with NAD(H) preferred over NADP(H); Km(DHAP) 8.1 uM, Km(NADH) 16 uM, Km(G1P) 1,370 uM, Km(NAD+) 59.3 uM; nickel-dependent homodimer
context: recombinant B. subtilis enzyme in vitro
limits: In vitro kinetics; no in vivo flux measurement

citation: This work, thermodynamic and Michaelis-Menten directionality calculation using the kinetics of PMID 18558723 and metabolite pools of PMID 19561621 and PMID 35767906
claim: AraM consumes G1P under arabinose growth
finding: Km(G1P)/Km(DHAP) = 169. Measured B. subtilis G1P is about 6 uM (30 uM total glycerophosphate, G3P:G1P = 4:1), which is 0.0044 x Km, 228-fold below saturation, while DHAP is 46 x Km, NADH 5.2 x Km and NAD+ 44 x Km. Forward/reverse one-way flux ratio = 1,382 to 66,795 across dG'o = -16.9 to -26.9 kJ/mol, with dG' = -18.7 to -28.7 kJ/mol. Equilibrium would require G1P in the tens of mM
context: in silico, using E. coli glucose-minimal nucleotide and DHAP pools as the closest available surrogate
limits: DHAP, NAD+ and NADH concentrations are from E. coli, not B. subtilis, and not from arabinose-grown cells

citation: This work, KEGG reaction census for DHAP (C00111) in B. subtilis
claim: L-arabinose catabolism produces or consumes DHAP in an arabinose-specific step
finding: DHAP participates in 39 KEGG reactions; in B. subtilis only fbaA, tpiA, gpsA, BSU09300, methylglyoxal synthase, nadA, iolJ and araM itself. araA, araB, araD and araL have no DHAP reaction. Arabinose ends at D-xylulose-5-phosphate and reaches DHAP only through the pentose phosphate pathway into F6P/G3P and then FbaA and TpiA, which are shared with glucose catabolism
limits: Pathway-database reasoning, not a flux measurement; a quantitative change in DHAP or NADH pool on arabinose was not measured by anyone retrievable

citation: Sa-Nogueira et al., araM dispensability (recorded as prior knowledge)
finding: araM is dispensable for growth on L-arabinose
limits: Growth on a single carbon source is a coarse phenotype; subtler defects were not assayed

citation: Guldan et al. 2011 / Linde et al. 2016, PMID 27226549
claim: The G1P made by AraM feeds PcrB-dependent ether lipid synthesis
finding: Heptaprenylglyceryl phosphate, the PcrB product derived from G1P, is dephosphorylated and acetylated in vivo, with YvoF as the acetyltransferase
limits: Does not itself trace the carbon back to AraM

claim: G1P exists as a measurable pool and reaches membrane phospholipid
finding: Total G3P plus G1P about 30 uM with a 4:1 G3P:G1P ratio; chiral chromatography found both enantiomers in the glycerol backbone of some phosphatidylglycerol species
context: B. subtilis and other Gram-positive bacteria
limits: No araM deletion was tested, so the cellular G1P pool is not formally attributed to AraM

claim: A route exists for G1P into bulk phospholipid
finding: PlsY and PlsC accept both stereo-forms of glycerol phosphate while PlsB is strictly G3P-specific
limits: Stereo-promiscuity in vitro does not establish in vivo flux magnitude

citation: This work, QuickGO annotation retrieval for P94527
claim: Current GO annotation of egsA reflects the experimental record
finding: All 5 annotations are IEA: GO:0050492 (GO_REF:0000120), GO:0106357 and GO:0106358 (RHEA, GO_REF:0000116), GO:0006650 (GO_REF:0000104), GO:0005737 (GO_REF:0000120). No experimental annotation exists despite the direct assay in PMID 18558723, and no arabinose-related term is attached

claim: Every cistron of the ara operon serves arabinose catabolism
finding: AraL is a low-specificity sugar phosphatase proposed to clear accidentally accumulated phosphorylated metabolites, and is translationally restrained by an mRNA structure
limits: Establishes a precedent inside the same operon, not a direct statement about araM
